templates_considered: no_destructive_sql (SEC-010): covers truncate and raw SQL, not db.del; does not fit delete ask
writes_check_first (BIZ-001): stack.statement_order for precondition before writes, but scoped to queries; does not fit tool approval gate
endpoints_need_login (AUTH-010), object.auth_required: agent tools are not endpoints; does not fit
tokens_expire, admin_endpoints_check_role, protected_endpoints_run_middleware, etc.: no overlap with ask

rules.covers: agents can't email customers without human approval

ask_parts_not_covered.part: agents shouldn't be able to call tools not explicitly given to them
delete ask scoped to only deletes via agent tools; deletes elsewhere (functions, endpoints) are not the agent's concern and were not scoped in

assumptions: 'Delete anything' means db.del / db.bulk.delete reached from agent tools; other destructive statements (db.truncate, raw SQL) are covered by existing template SEC-010, not added here
'Email customers' means util.send_email; api.request to an email vendor was not in scope
request_human_approval throws unless approval_id is approved, so a before-call that precedes the send is a real gate only if the tool passes approval_id
Agent tool scope = object_kinds tool; agent objects have no stack and are not inspected by these checks
New policies start active and advisory per skill guidance
confusions: Skill says a policy file 'carries no comments' but the workspace .xs files use // comments; unclear whether any policy header comments are allowed (I wrote none)
No check for 'agent may only call explicitly listed tools'; had to decide the ask is uncoverable rather than approximate it
stack.statement_order for approval gating checks that a call precedes the send, not that the approval is valid; the skill does not say whether the target function's own throw counts as a guarantee
Unclear whether object_kinds 'tool' with statement_forbidden follows called functions the same way as tool stacks (the check says called functions are followed, but tool-to-tool or middleware is not)
The catalogue's statements list is not enumerated anywhere I could find, so I took db.del and db.bulk.delete from workspace code, not from a documented list
wished_for: A check for an agent's tool allowlist (only tools listed on the agent may be used), or a documented agent-level tools check
A recipe for approval gating: how to express 'human approves before a side effect' using stack.statement_order with a function call
A list of statement names (db.del, db.bulk.delete, util.send_email, etc.) to avoid guessing from code
An example of agent-kind scoping, e.g. how to scope a rule to tools reached by a given agent
why_confidence: Delete and email-approval asks map to real checks and parse cleanly, but the approval gate only proves a call precedes the send, not that approval was granted; the tool-allowlist ask has no check; nothing evaluated against the workspace yet
